title: Pre-Analysis — Scene Control Extension of the Solid State Ceiling and Wall Wash Lighting

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Pre-analysis of a proposal to extend the solid state lighting scene control to serve cabin connectivity and crew applications, handed to the cabin systems programme when the overlap with the connectivity candidate became the dominant question.

sections.objective: Assess a proposal to open the lighting scene controller to a wider set of cabin applications, so that scenes can be driven from crew devices rather than only from the cabin intercommunication panel. The pre-analysis was asked to identify what already claims that interface, what the change does to the fleet still at the fluorescent standard, and whether the published cabin content can describe two controller behaviours without a second figure and a second procedure.
sections.findings_summary: Five items were confirmed and together they moved the question out of the lighting domain. The controller interface the proposal wants to open is already claimed by the connectivity server candidate, which places a wireless access point on the same ceiling supply and reads the same cabin data bus; the two proposals are solving overlapping problems with different hardware and neither dossier referenced the other. The superseded fluorescent standard is still flying on part of the fleet and its ballast items remain in the same part list figure, so any controller behaviour change has to be readable against both. The earlier ballast bulletin's effectivity becomes harder to interpret again. The cargo compartment lighting served by the same controller is also touched by a candidate blanket installation. On that basis the work order was handed to the cabin systems programme rather than concluded in the lighting chapter.
sections.next_steps: Transfer the analysis file to the cabin systems programme with the connectivity candidate as the receiving dossier, and ask that the scene control interface be specified once for both. Keep the lighting chapter as a contributor rather than the owner. Before any interface work starts, confirm with publications that the part list figure can carry the fluorescent and solid state configurations plus a controller behaviour variant, and if it cannot, split the figure first.

similarity_seeds: cabin scene control driven from a crew device instead of a panel
ceiling supply shared between lighting and a wireless access point
two lighting configurations in one part list figure

tasks.title: Search candidate cabin modifications claiming the same controller interface
Assess the fleet still at the fluorescent standard
Review the part list figure and cabin installation content
Confirm ceiling supply loading with the connectivity design team

expected_findings.rationale: The connectivity candidate installs a ceiling access point on the same supply and reads the same cabin data bus that the scene control proposal wants to open. Two dossiers are specifying the same interface from opposite ends and neither refers to the other.
expected_findings.resolution: Hand the interface specification to the cabin systems programme and let one dossier own it.

expected_findings.rationale: The superseded fluorescent standard is still flying on a material part of the fleet. Any controller behaviour change has to be described against an aircraft that has no controller at all, which the current documentation does not do.
expected_findings.resolution: State the fluorescent configuration explicitly as out of scope in whichever dossier takes the interface forward.

expected_findings.rationale: The ballast bulletin is effective on pre solid state aircraft. A third behaviour on the post conversion aircraft makes its exclusion clause read as though it also excludes aircraft it should still cover.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-state the exclusion clause in terms of the conversion rather than in terms of the controller.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries both lighting generations already. A controller behaviour variant is a third dimension that the alternate item notation cannot express without a second figure.
expected_findings.resolution: Split the figure before any interface change is published.

expected_findings.rationale: The cargo compartment lighting served by the same controller shares its mounting with the candidate blanket installation, so a controller change and a lining change would arrive in the same compartment at the same time.
expected_findings.resolution: Flag the interaction to the blanket candidate's own pre-analysis.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by the semantic pass on cabin comfort language and shares the overhead zone, but it retrofits an air cycle machine silencer and decoupled mount. It shares no part number, no functional item number and no controller interface with the lighting installation.

type_data.conclusion: Closed by delegation. The dominant question is an interface owned by two dossiers at once, which the lighting chapter cannot settle alone; the file was transferred to the cabin systems programme with the connectivity candidate as the receiving dossier.
